correctness.rationale: The rational map has poles only at 2±i√2, outside Markov spectra, and preserves rows because r(0)=1. Its first five Taylor coefficients a0..a4 are positive while a5=−1/108. All distinct-state transitions for arbitrary generators on ≤5 states have shortest paths of length ≤4, with first surviving coefficient a_d(Q^d)ij positive; inaccessible pairs remain zero, diagonals start at 1. A directed six-cycle gives a negative h5/108 leading entry. Exact circulant inversion supplies common positive D6 and N5=h5 p(h); all other entries have certified positive polynomial forms, including exact Bernstein coefficients and shifted polynomial for the diagonal. p increases strictly on h≥0, with one positive root. Fourier modes imply eventual positivity for every directed cycle n≥6. The delivered SymPy script reconstructed these equalities and verified the exact rational witness at h=1/10. The infinite-generator statement is proved analytically, not by enumeration.

value.rationale: This is a motivated structural minimal-state question for preservation of Markov probabilities under a standard third-order A-stable integrator. The smallest conservative nonreversible obstruction is an irreducible homogeneous six-cycle, and its complete positive-step set is a nontrivial disconnected interval rather than an isolated negative example. The sharp algebraic cutoff permits a natural reproducible six-state benchmark and contrasts substantively with the earlier six-vertex undirected path and eight-state fourth-order Padé cases. No inflated downstream performance or certification claim is made.
